narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which estimated a 58% probability that you represent a bad credit risk — a figure just above the threshold needed for approval, meaning the decision was not overwhelmingly negative, but still resulted in a denial. Several aspects of your current financial profile combined to push the assessment in an unfavorable direction, and understanding these factors can help you take concrete steps toward a successful application in the future.

Counterfactual scenarios are "what if" analyses that show the minimum changes to your situation that would have flipped the model's decision from denied to approved. Think of them as alternative versions of your application where one or more things are different — and the outcome changes as a result. In your case, three such scenarios were generated, and they tell a remarkably consistent story.

Across all three counterfactual scenarios, only a single feature needed to change to turn your application from a denial into an approval: the status of your checking account. In every scenario without exception, your checking account status shifted from being overdrawn (below 0 DM) to having no checking account at all. Every other aspect of your profile — the loan duration, credit history, loan purpose, amount requested, savings, employment situation, installment rate, and all other factors — remained exactly the same across all three scenarios. This is a striking finding: the model's entire objection to your application appears to hinge on this one factor.

Currently, your checking account is in a negative balance, which is a significant red flag for credit assessments. Among applicants who were approved, only about 20% had a negative checking account balance, while roughly 50% had no checking account at all — the very status that appears in all three approval scenarios. Having an overdrawn account signals financial stress and instability to the model, and it appears to outweigh other concerns in your profile.

It is worth acknowledging that your profile does carry other risk signals: you are currently unemployed, your loan duration of 42 months is more than double the average of 19 months seen among approved applicants, and your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the approved average of roughly 3%. Your loan purpose — home repairs — is also among the less common reasons for approved loans. However, the model's analysis suggests that none of these factors alone, or even in combination, were the deciding issue — the overdrawn checking account was.

The most actionable step you can take is to resolve the negative balance in your checking account before reapplying. If closing or restructuring that account brings it to a neutral standing, the model's scenarios suggest this single change could be sufficient to secure approval, even without altering your loan amount, duration, or any other aspect of your application. While longer-term improvements — such as securing employment or reducing the requested loan term — would further strengthen your profile, the immediate priority is clear: address the checking account situation first.
